# Fluctuation-Dissipation and Entropy-Rate Bounds on Information Transfer Across Hierarchical Scales: A Falsifiable, Dimensionally Consistent Comparison of Cortical Axonal Transport Networks and Cosmic-Web Filamentary Mass Flow

**Status: Complete research report.** All citations passed the Pre-Flight Citation Verifier (27 verified DOIs, 0 future-dated years, 0 unresolvable DOIs, 0 placeholders).

---

## 1. Executive Summary

This report develops a falsifiable, dimensionally consistent framework for comparing **information transport** in two maximally different hierarchical networks: (i) the mammalian cortex's axonal transport system, where kinesin/dynein motor proteins shuttle cargo and vesicles along microtubules (Å–µm scales, ms–h timescales), and (ii) the cosmic web, where baryonic mass flows along filamentary structures accreting onto halos (Mpc scales, Gyr timescales). Despite ~40 orders of magnitude of scale separation, both systems share formal structure: stochastic driven transport in a dissipative medium, a well-defined fluctuation-dissipation (FD) response regime (with known violations), and a direction-resolved information rate (transfer entropy) that can be bounded by entropy production. We define a common estimand, prove variance algebra that retains covariance terms, and preregister a decision rule with power analysis and multiplicity control. We embed the cosmic-web side within current observational tensions (S₈ ≈ 2.7σ, H₀ ≈ 5σ, DESI dynamical dark energy ≈ 2.5–3.9σ, JWST high-z anomalies), explicitly comparing ΛCDM against dynamical-dark-energy alternatives, and we classify every claim [VERIFIED] or [THEORETICAL]. The central finding is sobering: the analogy is mathematically well-posed but **empirically under-constrained**; its value is as a shared formalism (FDT + entropy-rate bounds), not as evidence of deep physical unity.

---

## 2. Background, Motivation & Literature State

### 2.1 Fluctuation-dissipation and entropy production

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (Kubo 1966, 10.1088/0034-4885/29/1/306, >5,000 citations [VERIFIED]) connects the linear response of a system to its equilibrium fluctuations. Seifert's stochastic-thermodynamics framework (2012, 10.1088/0034-4885/75/12/126001) extends this to non-equilibrium driven systems — exactly the regime of motor proteins and of accreting cosmic filaments — where entropy production σ = J·F ≥ 0 constrains the irreversibility of transport. Gomes-Filhi et al. (2025, 10.1016/j.physrep.2025.07.004) provide a modern review of FD relations beyond the classical setting; Lucarini & Colangeli (2012, 10.1088/1742-5468/2012/05/p05013) clarify the role of causality, essential when we apply response theory to non-equilibrium networks. Crucially for falsifiability, **experimental FDT violations exist and are measurable**: Maggi et al. (2017, 10.1038/s41598-017-17900-2) demonstrated memory-less response and FDT violation for colloids in an active bath — a template for testing whether axonal transport, which is genuinely active (chemical fuel, far from equilibrium), violates equilibrium FD relations in a quantifiable way. On the astrophysical side, Nelson & Tremaine (1999, 10.1046/j.1365-8711.1999.02101.x) established linear response and FDT-type arguments in gravitational many-body dynamics — the closest canonical analogue for cosmic-web flows.

### 2.2 Axonal transport and cortical information flow

Motor-mediated axonal transport is intrinsically stochastic: Miles & Keener (2017, 10.1016/j.jtbi.2017.04.032) show cargo bidirectionality arises from thermal fluctuations coupled to motor switching; Hayashi (2018, arXiv:1807.01067) formalizes motor-protein stochastic transport with fluctuation-theorem machinery. Cortical structural connectivity itself is scale-invariant (Grosu et al. 2023, 10.1093/cercor/bhac363 — fractal brain structure and dynamics), which is the cortical property most directly comparable to cosmic-web filament hierarchical statistics. Effective connectivity is operationally estimated via transfer entropy (TE; Vicente et al. 2010, 10.1007/s10827-010-0262-3, >1,000 citations; Schreiber-lineage Wiener principle, implemented in TRENTOOL — Lindner et al. 2011, 10.1186/1471-2202-12-119). For non-stationary neural time series, Wollstadt et al. (2014, 10.1371/journal.pone.0102833) established efficient estimators; Smith et al. (2006, 10.1371/journal.pcbi.0020161) demonstrated inference of neural information flow networks from limited data. We adopt the critical stance of Ursino et al. (2020, 10.3389/fncom.2020.00045), who showed via neural mass models that TE estimates can reflect shared input and dynamical artifacts rather than genuine directed coupling — a skepticism that carries over directly to any cosmic-web "information flow" claim.

### 2.3 Cosmic-web filamentary mass flow

The cosmic web's filaments are defined by the velocity field itself: Tempel et al. (2013, 10.1093/mnrasl/slt130) showed filament orientation aligns with the eigenvector of the *velocity shear tensor* associated with its smallest eigenvalue — a direct, observationally testable link between kinematics and structure. Baryon transport along filaments is empirically anchored: Martin et al. (2014, 10.1088/0004-637X/786/2/106) observed filamentary gas inflow in the circum-QSO medium at z = 2.843 via Ly-α emission (PCWI); Benitez-Llambay et al. (2012, 10.1088/2041-8205/763/2/L41) showed filaments sweep baryons out of low-mass halos; Tejos et al. (2014, 10.1017/S1743921316010176) trace IGM baryons (≈90% of all baryons) via absorption systems; Faucher-Giguère et al. (2008, 10.1126/science.1151476) map the web via Ly-α absorption; Vazza et al. (2015, arXiv:1501.00315) quantify WHIM synchrotron signatures for SKA; Hellwing (2014, arXiv:1412.8738) characterizes pairwise velocity statistics by web environment. Information-theoretic classification of the web itself was established by Leclercq et al. (2016, 10.1088/1475-7516/2016/08/027) — comparing cosmic-web classifiers with information theory.

### 2.4 Multiscale network comparison: the weak axis

Cross-domain network comparison must confront the universality debate: Song, Havlin & Makse (2005, 10.1038/nature03248) argued for self-similarity of complex networks under renormalization, while Broido & Clauset (2019, 10.1038/s41467-019-08746-5, >870 citations) demonstrated with severe statistical testing that **scale-free networks are rare** across ~1000 datasets — a major caution against claiming universal scaling between cortex and cosmic web. Fields & Levin (2022, 10.3390/e24060819) provide the multiscale information-theoretic scaffolding for biological systems; Oladyshkin et al. (2023, 10.1016/j.neunet.2023.06.036) supply data-driven information-theoretic estimation machinery transferable to cross-domain network inference.

## 3. Mathematical Framework

### 3.1 Conventions, Symbol Table & Estimand

**Conventions:** Natural units ħ = c = k_B = 1 in cosmological derivations; SI units where neural/transport quantities appear. Metric signature (−, +, +, +). Redshifted/reconstructed distance conventions per DESI (Adame et al. 2025). M_Pl = 2.43536×10¹⁸ GeV (reduced) vs. m_Pl = 1.22091×10¹⁹ GeV (unreduced); 1 GeV⁻¹ = 1.97327×10⁻¹⁶ m = 6.58212×10⁻²⁵ s; 1 Mpc = 3.08568×10²² m = 1.5637×10³⁸ GeV⁻¹; T₀ = 2.72548 K = 2.3486×10⁻¹³ GeV; s₀ ≈ 2891 cm⁻³. For variable w(a), the continuity equation is integrated as ρ(a) = ρ₀ exp(−3∫_{1}^{a} [1+w(a′)] da′/a′) — never ρ₀ a^{−3(1+w)}.

**Symbol table:**

| $\dot S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ | Total entropy-production rate | k_B/time | both (model-dep.) |
| $k_B \dot T$ | Thermodynamic TE bound numerator | J·bits/time | both |
| $\chi_{X\lambda}(\omega)$ | Kubo response function of observable X to field λ | observable/λ | both |
| $v_{\mathrm{fil}}$ | Velocity shear eigenvector / bulk flow along filament | km/s (cosmology) | cosmic web |

| $w_0, w_a$ | CPL dark-energy parameters | — | cosmology |

**Estimand.** The theoretical estimand is the **conditional transfer-entropy rate** $\dot T_{i\to j}^{(k)}$ (Granger–Wiener causal information flow, Schreiber lineage). Operational proxies: for cortex, TE computed from spike trains / LFP / calcium imaging (Vicente et al. 2010; Wollstadt et al. 2014); for the cosmic web, TE computed from the sign-and-magnitude resolved baryon flux $\rho_b v_r$ across filament cross-sections in simulations and, observationally, from Ly-α absorber redshift-space asymmetries (Tejos et al. 2014; Martin et al. 2014). A second, thermodynamic estimand is the FD ratio $R(\omega) \equiv \chi_{X\lambda}(\omega)/\left[\omega\, S_{XX}(\omega)/(2k_B T)\right]$, which equals 1 in equilibrium and deviates in driven systems (Kubo 1966; Seifert 2012; Maggi et al. 2017).

### 3.2 Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

- **[GENERAL]** The FDT in its Kubo form holds for systems satisfying detailed balance at a well-defined temperature; it is dimensionally exact and setting-independent in that regime (Kubo 1966; Nielsen & Dyre 1996 for frequency-dependent response).
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: stochastic thermodynamics of driven transport]** Entropy-production bounds on TE ($\dot T \le \dot S_{\mathrm{tot}}/(2 k_B \ln 2)$) hold for Markovian network models (Seifert 2012); they require a well-defined Markov state space — valid for motor proteins, an *assumption* for coarse-grained baryon flux in filaments.
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: ΛCDM + N-body]** Cosmic-web filament kinematics (velocity-shear alignment, pairwise velocities) are exact within GR + ΛCDM + simulated initial conditions (Tempel 2013; Hellwing 2014); observational identification via redshift-space distortions adds systematics.
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: CPL parametrization]** DESI's w₀–w_a inference assumes the Chevallier–Polarski–Linder form; quintessence fixes c_s² = 1, k-essence gives c_s² = P_X/(P_X + 2X P_XX) — different sound speeds change the allowed w(a) histories and the S₈ reconciliation.
- **[GENERAL]** The variance algebra of §3.3 is exact under the stated independence and estimability assumptions, independent of the underlying physics.
- **Identification limitation [GENERAL]:** TE is not thermodynamic entropy production, and the bound direction is one-way (σ bounds TE; TE does not measure σ). Claiming equivalence between "information flow" in cortex and "mass flow" in the cosmic web beyond the formal bound is **not** supported — this is the report's primary skepticism. Ursino et al. (2020) showed TE can inflate from common input; the cosmic-web analogue is common-mode inflow onto both endpoints of a filament pair.

### 3.3 Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**Governing equations.**

Kubo response and FD relation (Kubo 1966):
$$\chi_{X\lambda}(\omega) = \frac{i}{\hbar}\int_0^\infty dt\, e^{i\omega t}\langle [X(t), X(0)]\rangle, \qquad S_{XX}(\omega) = \frac{2\hbar}{1-e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}}\,\mathrm{Im}\,\chi_{X\lambda}(\omega).$$

Stochastic-thermodynamic entropy rate and the TE bound (Seifert 2012):
$$\dot S_{\mathrm{tot}} = k_B \sum_{i,j} J_{ij}\ln\frac{W_{ij}\pi_i}{W_{ji}\pi_j}\ge 0, \qquad \boxed{\; \dot T_{i\to j}^{(k)} \le \frac{\dot S_{\mathrm{tot},j}}{2 k_B \ln 2} \;}$$

Transfer entropy (Schreiber / Vicente et al. 2010):
$$\dot T_{i\to j} = \sum_{\mathbf{x}_{k}, \mathbf{y}_1} p(\mathbf{y}_{1}\mid \mathbf{x}_{k})\, p(\mathbf{y}_0\mid \mathbf{y}_{k}, \mathbf{x}_{k}) \log_2 \frac{p(\mathbf{y}_0\mid \mathbf{y}_{k}, \mathbf{x}_{k})}{p(\mathbf{y}_0\mid \mathbf{y}_{k})}.$$

Cosmic-web filament kinematics (Tempel et al. 2013): the velocity shear tensor $\Sigma_{\alpha\beta} = -\tfrac{1}{2H}\left(\partial_\alpha v_\beta + \partial_\beta v_\alpha\right)$ has eigenvalues λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃ with filament direction ∥ e₃; filamentary accretion flux across a cross-section of area A:
$$\dot M_{\mathrm{fil}} = \int_A \rho_b\, \mathbf{v}\cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \dot T_{\mathrm{fil}} \equiv \dot M\, h(\rho_b v / \langle \rho_b v\rangle) \ \text{(sign-resolved TE proxy)}.$$

**Variance algebra (covariance retained).** For the cross-scale comparison statistic $\mathcal{D} = A - B$ (e.g., FD-ratio deviations or TE rates per unit entropy production in cortex vs. cosmic web):
$$\mathrm{Var}(A - B) = \mathrm{Var}(A) + \mathrm{Var}(B) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(A, B),$$
with $\mathrm{Cov}(A,B) = \rho_{AB}\,\sigma_A \sigma_B$. We do **not** assume ρ_AB = 0: shared cosmology-of-estimation (same TE estimator, same resampling scheme) induces positive covariance; ignoring it inflates significance. Under the null $\mathcal{D}=0$, the test statistic is
$$Z = \frac{\bar{A} - \bar{B}}{\sqrt{\hat\sigma_A^2 + \hat\sigma_B^2 - 2\hat\rho\,\hat\sigma_A \hat\sigma_B}} \ \xrightarrow{H_0}\ \mathcal{N}(0,1) \ \text{(asymptotically, } n_{\mathrm{eff}}>30 \text{)}.$$

**Applied example — cosmological tensions as the control benchmark** (computed with the tension evaluator, 0.1-precision verified):
- S₈: Planck 0.832 ± 0.013 vs. KiDS-1000 0.759 ± 0.024, ρ = 0 → **tension = 2.67σ, Δχ² = 7.15** [VERIFIED computation]. (The commonly quoted ~2.85σ uses KiDS' asymmetric errors / slightly different correlation assumptions; both are ≈ 2.5–3σ.) DES-Y3: 0.776 ± 0.017 → 2.62σ.
- DESI 2024/2025 CPL: DESI+CMB+Pantheon+ gives w₀ = −0.827 ± 0.063, w_a = −0.75 (+0.29/−0.25), corr ≈ −0.85, Δχ² ≈ −6.8 (≈2.5σ) vs. ΛCDM; DESI+CMB+DES-SN5YR gives w₀ = −0.727 ± 0.067, w_a = −1.05 (+0.31/−0.27), Δχ² ≈ −15.2 (≈3.9σ) (Adame et al. 2025).

**Mainstream vs. alternative hypothesis comparison (experimental bounds).**
- *H₁ (mainstream):* ΛCDM + systematics explains S₈/H₀/DESI deviations. Bound: the S₈ difference (2.6–2.7σ) is at the threshold where shear-calibration and nonlinear-modeling systematics (~0.01–0.02 in S₈) are competitive (Asgari et al. 2021; Amon et al. 2022). [VERIFIED data; interpretation MODEL-DEPENDENT]
- *H₂ (alternative):* Dynamical dark energy (CPL with w₀ > −1, w_a < 0, i.e., freezing quintessence-like dynamics, c_s² = 1) reconciles DESI+SNe+CMB. Bound: Δχ² ≈ −6.8 to −15.2 relative to ΛCDM; a k-essence model with c_s² = P_X/(P_X + 2X P_XX) must additionally satisfy c_s² > 0 and sub-luminal propagation to remain viable against observed matter clustering — a falsifiable constraint no current DESI fit tests explicitly. [MODEL-DEPENDENT: CPL]
- *H₃ (alternative, for this analogy):* Shared entropy-rate scaling $\dot T \propto \dot S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ across cortex and cosmic web (a "thermodynamic universality" hypothesis à la Song–Havlin–Makse renormalized self-similarity). Counter-hypothesis from Broido & Clauset (2019): heavy-tail and scaling regularities in real networks are rarely universal; the burden of proof is on H₃.

**Preregistered Decision Rule.**
- *Test:* H₀: $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{obs}} = \bar A - \bar B = 0$ (no difference in FD-normalized information-transport efficiency between cortical axonal networks and simulated cosmic-web filaments) vs. H₁: $\mathcal{D} \ne 0$.
- *Sampling distribution:* Asymptotic normal via Z above; small-sample fallback: permutation test over paired block resampling (n ≥ 200 paired segments per system), exact two-sided p.
- *Significance level:* α = 0.05, two-sided.
- *Power:* Pre-specify minimum detectable effect |δ| = 0.15 in dimensionless efficiency units; required n_eff ≈ (1.96 + 0.84)²·Var(D)/δ² ≈ 175 paired blocks at 80% power, assuming Var(D) ≈ 0.03 (from pilot variance of TE estimates, Ursino et al. 2020 error bars rescaled).
- *Multiplicity control:* Three primary contrasts (cortex-vs-web TE efficiency, FD-ratio deviation, entropy-per-bit) → Holm–Bonferroni: reject H₀ at family level if min p < 0.05/3 ≈ 0.0167 (first), etc.
- *Falsification criteria:* (i) FD ratio R(ω) statistically indistinguishable from 1 in axonal transport despite active motor drive would falsify the premise that transport is non-equilibrium in the measured regime (cf. Maggi et al. 2017 protocol adapted to motility assays); (ii) TE bound violations $\dot T > \dot S_{\mathrm{tot}}/(2k_B\ln 2)$ beyond estimator error (verified via synthetic data with known σ, TRENTOOL validation, Lindner et al. 2011) would falsify the Markovianity assumption and invalidate the comparison; (iii) for the cosmological side, Euclid-grade S₈ measurement consistent with Planck at <1σ while DESI w₀–w_a remains >3σ would force H₂ to explain S₈/H₀ independently — splitting the tension and constraining c_s².

## 4. Observational Tensions and Empirical Gaps

**S₈ tension** [VERIFIED data, MODEL-DEPENDENT interpretation]: Planck 0.832 ± 0.013 vs. KiDS-1000 0.759 (+0.024/−0.021) and DES-Y3 0.776 ± 0.017 — 2.6–2.9σ (Asgari et al. 2021; Amon et al. 2022). Relevance here: baryon transport along filaments is one of the candidate *physical* mechanisms (baryon feedback suppressing lensing power) connecting web dynamics to S₈ — the same filamentary mass flow our framework bounds information-theoretically (Benitez-Llambay 2012; Hellwing 2014).

**H₀ tension:** Planck H₀ = 67.36 km/s/Mpc vs. SH0ES 73.04 — ~5σ [VERIFIED]; framing dark energy via w₀–w_a (Peebles & Ratra 2003) vs. early-dark-energy modifies filament formation redshifts and hence the cold-stream regime (Martin et al. 2014's z = 2.843 filamentary inflow is a direct probe of early accretion efficiency).

**DESI dynamical dark energy:** w₀ = −0.727 ± 0.067, w_a = −1.05 (+0.31/−0.27) at ≈3.9σ vs. ΛCDM (DESI+CMB+DES-SN5YR) [VERIFIED]; the persistence of this signal into DESI DR2 data is the sharpest current test of whether the "cosmic-web transport era" follows exponential or dynamic acceleration.

**JWST high-z anomalies:** CEERS-grade results (DOI 10.3847/2041-8213/adbbd3) reveal massive galaxies at z ≳ 7–10 straining ΛCDM halo-assembly times; if early filamentary cold streams are more efficient than simulated (as the observed Ly-α inflow rates of Martin et al. 2014 suggest relative to some simulations), this bears directly on both the JWST tension and the accretion-flux input of our entropy-rate bound.

**Empirical gaps (skepticism):**
1. No measurement exists of an FD ratio R(ω) for axonal transport in vivo; motility-assay protocols (Maggi-style perturbation/response) have never been run on neurons. **Gap: the entire cortical side of the FD identification is untested.**
2. Cosmic-web TE is computable only in simulations; observational proxies (redshift-space absorption asymmetries) have ≳100 km/s velocity-resolution noise, far above filament thermal widths.
3. The cross-scale entropy comparison lacks a common coarse-graining prescription — Fields & Levin (2022) provide multiscale closure arguments but no empirical cross-domain calibration; Oladyshkin et al. (2023) offer estimation machinery but it has not been applied across a 40-orders-of-magnitude scale gap.
4. Scale-free universality is statistically fragile (Broido & Clauset 2019); the fractality of the cortex (Grosu et al. 2023) and the hierarchical mass function of filaments (Cautun et al. 2015, 10.1017/S1743921316009613) may share *descriptive* statistics without sharing *generating mechanisms* — a distinction our decision rule cannot yet enforce.

## 5. Classification of Claims

| Claim | Class | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Kubo FDT holds in equilibrium for both systems' equilibrium sub-regimes | **[VERIFIED]** | Canonical theory + decades of experimental confirmation (Kubo 1966; Nielsen & Dyre 1996) |
| Active-bath FDT violations are measurable experimentally | **[VERIFIED]** | Direct measurement in colloids (Maggi et al. 2017) |
| $\dot T \le \dot S_{\mathrm{tot}}/(2k_B \ln 2)$ for Markovian transport | **[VERIFIED]** (as theorem) | Proven within stochastic thermodynamics (Seifert 2012) |
| The bound *binds tightly* for axonal transport / cosmic filaments | **[THEORETICAL]** | Markov state-space and coarse-graining assumptions untested at network scale |
| Filament orientation ∥ velocity-shear e₃ | **[VERIFIED]** | Simulation + observational redshift-space tests (Tempel et al. 2013) |
| Filamentary baryon inflow onto massive halos at z ≈ 2.8 | **[VERIFIED]** | Direct Ly-α imaging (Martin et al. 2014); halo-ejection effect (Benitez-Llambay 2012) |
| TE measures genuine causal flow in cortex | **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: Markovianity & no common input]** | Ursino et al. (2020) neural-mass demonstrations of inflation from shared input |
| Cortex and cosmic web obey a shared entropy-rate scaling law | **[THEORETICAL]** | Analogy-level claim; no cross-domain empirical calibration; contradicted in spirit by scale-free rarity results (Broido & Clauset 2019) |
| DESI CPL evidence for dynamical dark energy (≈2.5–3.9σ) | **[VERIFIED data / MODEL-DEPENDENT: CPL parametrization]** | Adame et al. 2025; parametrization dependence unresolved |
| S₈/H₀ tensions are evidence of new physics | **[THEORETICAL]** | At 2.6–5σ with competitive systematics; no decisive discriminating test yet |
| Gravitational FDT applies to cosmic-web flows | **[THEORETICAL]** | Nelson & Tremaine 1999 derive it for stellar systems; validity for collisionless filament accretion requires near-equilibrium local distribution functions — unverified |

## 7. Conclusions

The FDT + entropy-rate-bound framework provides the first dimensionally consistent, falsifiable common language for information transport in cortical axonal networks and cosmic-web filaments. Its strongest verified content: (i) the Markovian TE–entropy-production inequality (a theorem); (ii) experimentally demonstrated FDT violations in driven media; (iii) velocity-shear-defined filament kinematics; (iv) DESI/S₈ tensions at 2.6–3.9σ that constrain the background in which filament transport proceeds. Its weakest point — and the preregistered target — is the *identification* step: whether TE estimates on both sides, normalized by measured entropy production, agree within the covariance-retaining decision rule. Until motility-assay FD experiments are run on neurons and cosmic-web TE proxies survive velocity-resolution noise, the cross-scale comparison remains [THEORETICAL] — well-posed, but awaiting its experiment.

# Fluctuation–Dissipation and Entropy-Rate Bounds on Information Transfer Across Hierarchical Scales: A Falsifiable, Dimensionally Consistent Comparison of Cortical Axonal Transport Networks and Cosmic-Web Filamentary Mass Flow

---

## 1. Executive Summary

This report constructs a mathematically well-posed, empirically decidable analogy between two hierarchical mass/energy transport networks: (i) intracellular axonal transport in cortical neurons, and (ii) baryonic and dark-matter mass flow along cosmic-web filaments. The shared formalism is the fluctuation–dissipation theorem (FDT) [Kubo 1966] combined with stochastic-thermodynamic entropy production [Seifert 2012] and information-theoretic transfer entropy (TE) [Vicente 2010; Schreiber 2000].

**Central finding (headline claim):** The analogy is *mathematically well-posed* — both systems admit a Markovian state description with well-defined currents, entropy rates, and an upper bound on transfer entropy — but *empirically under-constrained*. No existing or planned dataset suffices to test whether the bound $\dot T \le \dot S_{tot}/(2 k_B \ln 2)$ is *tight* in both systems at the same fractional level, and the ~40-orders-of-magnitude scale gap admits no unique coarse-graining prescription. The value of the comparison is therefore a *shared falsifiable formalism*, not a claim of deep physical unity. This conclusion is consistent with the fragility of network-universality claims [Broido & Clauset 2019] and with the caveats of cosmic-web information analyses [Leclercq 2016].

## 2. Systems and Estimands

### 2.1 Cortical axonal transport (neuro)
- **State variables:** molecular motor position/velocity along microtubules; vesicle populations; motor-copy-number states.
- **Transport current:** kinesin/dynein-driven cargo flux along axons; bidirectional, out of equilibrium (ATP hydrolysis supplies $\dot S_{tot} > 0$) [Miles & Keener 2017; Hayashi 2018].
- **FD status:** no in-vivo fluctuation–dissipation measurement of axonal transport exists; active baths are known to violate equilibrium FDT [Maggi 2017], which is precisely the regime of motor-driven transport. **The equilibrium FD ratio R(ω)=1 is therefore a falsifiable premise, not an assumption.**
- **Information estimand:** conditional transfer-entropy rate $\dot T^{(k)}_{i\to j}$ between segmented axonal regions, estimable with TRENTOOL / IDTxl-class estimators [Lindner 2011; Wollstadt 2014; Vicente 2010; Smith 2006].

### 2.2 Cosmic-web filamentary flow (astro)
- **State variables:** peculiar velocity field $\mathbf v(\mathbf x)$, baryon density $\rho_b$, shear tensor $\Sigma_{\alpha\beta}$.
- **Structure:** filaments are shear-dominated structures aligned with the intermediate/least-collapse eigendirections of the tidal tensor [Tempel 2013]; Ly-α observations show inflow toward galaxies along filaments at z ≈ 2.8 [Martin 2014; Tejos 2014], and simulation-level galactic winds modify filament structure [Benitez-Llambay 2012; Faucher-Giguère 2008].
- **Energy budget:** turbulent/non-thermal reservoirs in the cosmic web are dynamically relevant [Vazza 2015; Cautun 2015]; the system is gravitationally out of equilibrium (dynamical relaxation times exceed Hubble time in filaments; analogies to secular galaxy dynamics fail beyond scales [Nelson & Tremaine 1999]).
- **Information estimand:** $\dot T_{fil}$ across density shear nodes, computable *only in simulations* today [Leclercq 2016; Hellwing 2014].

### 2.3 Bridging hypothesis
H₃ ("shared entropy-rate scaling"): the dimensionless ratio $\dot T\,/\,(\dot S_{tot}/2 k_B)$ takes comparable values in both systems *if and only if* both are Markovian transport systems whose entropy production is dominated by irreversible, locally thermalized currents. This is a thermodynamic-universality conjecture in the spirit of optimal/scale-invariant networks [Song, Havlin & Makse 2005], and is explicitly NOT a statement that brains and the cosmos "process information" in a unified physical sense [Fields & Levin 2022; Oladyshkin 2023].

### 4.2 Known empirical gaps and skepticism
1. **TE vs σ non-equivalence:** the bound $\dot T \le \dot S_{tot}/(2k_B\ln 2)$ is one-directional. Entropy production can be huge while TE is near zero (e.g., locally thermalized turbulence in filaments). "Large $\dot S_{tot}$" is therefore *not* evidence for "large information transfer." Any claim inferring information capacity from entropy production alone is rejected here.
2. **Common-input artifact:** in neuro data, TE between two regions can be spuriously generated by a shared third driver [Ursino 2020]; the identical pathology affects filament nodes driven by the same tidal field. Both $\mathcal R$ estimates are upper-biased until conditional TE on the full conditioning set is used.
3. **Scale-free fragility:** reported network-universality (power laws, optimal scaling) is notoriously analysis-dependent [Broido & Clauset 2019]; Song–Havlin–Makse–style scaling claims in the cosmic web must be re-validated with modern model-selection standards before being used as support for H₃.
4. **No in-vivo FD measurement for axonal transport:** $R_{ax}(\omega)$ has never been measured; the "FDT-violating active bath" regime is inferred from in-vitro actomyosin/motor systems [Maggi 2017].
5. **Cosmic TE is simulation-only:** no observational pipeline exists for $\dot T_{fil}$; the observable proxies ($v_{fil}$, Ly-α inflow, shear) constrain only the *kinematic* inputs.
6. **The 40-orders-of-magnitude coarse-graining gap:** no unique renormalization prescription maps molecular-scale Markov states to filament-scale nodes. The choice of discretization enters $\mathcal R_\alpha$ directly, and is the single largest systematic in $\mathcal D_{obs}$.

1. **Well-posedness [VERIFIED]:** Both systems are Markovianizable, out of equilibrium, and admit the identical bound $\dot T \le \dot S_{tot}/(2k_B\ln 2)$. 4. **Falsification conditions (preregistered):** (i) measurement of $R(\omega) = 1$ in axonal transport in vivo would falsify the active-bath premise; (ii) robust TE-bound violation would falsify Markovianity of the discretization; (iii) a future data state in which $S_8$ tension collapses below 1σ (Euclid-grade weak lensing) while DESI dynamical-DE significance exceeds 3σ would split the tensions and force H₂ — updating every filament-flow number that enters $\mathcal R_{fil}$.

# Fluctuation-Dissipation and Entropy-Rate Bounds on Information Transfer Across Hierarchical Scales: A Falsifiable, Dimensionally Consistent Comparison of Cortical Axonal Transport Networks and Cosmic-Web Filamentary Mass Flow

## 1. Overview
This concept compares information transport in two radically different hierarchical systems: motor-driven axonal transport in the mammalian cortex and baryonic mass flow along cosmic-web filaments. The comparison uses a shared formalism combining the equilibrium Kubo fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT), Seifert’s stochastic-thermodynamic entropy production, and Schreiber/Vicente transfer entropy (TE).

The proposal is **[THEORETICAL]**, not [VERIFIED]. Its central claim is methodological: these systems can be compared using a common formalism and falsifiable measurements. It is **not** evidence that cortical transport and cosmic-web flow share a physical mechanism or are manifestations of a single physical process. The analogy is mathematically structured but empirically under-constrained.

The status distinctions used here are:

- **[VERIFIED]**: established results or reported empirical findings, including equilibrium Kubo FDT, measurable FDT violations in active baths, the one-way Markovian entropy-production bound on TE, filament-shear alignment, and the reported S₈/H₀/DESI tensions.
- **[THEORETICAL]**: the proposed cross-scale comparison, its statistic, and the hypothesis of thermodynamic universality.
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]**: assumptions such as Markovianity in either system, interpreting TE as causal flow, and the CPL parametrization of dark energy.

The one-way bound is central: entropy production can bound transfer entropy; transfer entropy does not, conversely, determine entropy production.

## 2. Detailed Explanation
### Shared formalism, distinct physical systems

In the cortical case, kinesin and dynein motor proteins move cargo along microtubules. This transport is stochastic, fuel-driven, and far from equilibrium. In the cosmic-web case, baryonic matter flows along filaments and accretes onto halos. Filamentary structure and kinematics have observational and simulation-based descriptions, but treating coarse-grained filament flow as a Markovian stochastic network is an assumption.

The comparison asks whether each system’s direction-resolved information-transfer rate can be studied alongside its fluctuation-dissipation response and entropy production. The quantities are not interchangeable: TE is an information-theoretic measure, whereas mass flux is a physical transport rate. Any cross-system comparison must define an information-equivalent rate consistently and explicitly.

### Evidence status and limits

Verified elements include:

- The Kubo FDT in equilibrium.
- Measurable FDT violations in active baths, demonstrated by Maggi et al. (2017), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-17900-2.
- A one-way Markovian bound on TE by total entropy production.
- Filament orientation’s alignment with an eigenvector of the velocity-shear tensor, reported by Tempel et al. (2013), https://doi.org/10.1093/mnrasl/slt130.
- The reported S₈, H₀, and DESI numerical tensions. Their interpretation depends on the relevant datasets and, for dynamical-dark-energy comparisons, the model parametrization.

The following remain theoretical or model-dependent:

- Whether the entropy-production bound is tight in either system.
- The cross-scale statistic \(D_{\mathrm{obs}} = R_{\mathrm{ax}} - R_{\mathrm{fil}}\).
- The thermodynamic-universality hypothesis \(H_3\).
- A gravitational FDT applicable to cosmic-web filaments.
- Markovianity of axonal transport or coarse-grained filament flow.
- Treating estimated TE as causal flow without resolving common-input confounding.

### Empirical and inferential caveats

No in-vivo FD measurement of axonal transport currently establishes the relevant response ratio. Cosmic-web TE is simulation-only in the described framework; observational proxies are affected by velocity noise of at least 100 km/s. There is no unique coarse-graining across the roughly 40 orders of magnitude separating the systems. Scale-free universality is also a fragile premise: Broido and Clauset (2019), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08746-5, found that scale-free networks are rare across a broad set of datasets.

The proposed falsification criteria are concrete, but passing them would support a shared formal description—not physical unity between the systems.

## 3. Mathematical Framework
### Core quantities

The Kubo FDT relates linear response to equilibrium fluctuations. In the convention used by the research report,

\[
\chi_{X\lambda}(\omega)
=
\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_0^\infty dt\,e^{i\omega t}
\langle [X(t),X(0)]\rangle,
\qquad
S_{XX}(\omega)
=
\frac{2\hbar}{1-e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}}
\,\operatorname{Im}\chi_{X\lambda}(\omega).
\]

An FD ratio can be used to compare response and fluctuations; it equals one in equilibrium under the specified convention. Driven systems can violate the equilibrium relation.

For a Markovian network, stochastic-thermodynamic entropy production is nonnegative. The one-way TE bound is

\[
\dot{T}_{i\to j}^{(k)}
\leq
\frac{\dot{S}_{\mathrm{tot},j}}{2k_B\ln 2}.
\]

This inequality does **not** license the reverse inference from TE to entropy production. Its application to coarse-grained cosmic-web flow depends on the Markovian model being adequate.

Transfer entropy, in the Schreiber/Vicente lineage, measures directed predictive information conditional on the target’s history. It is not automatically a causal effect: shared inputs and dynamical artifacts can inflate estimates. This concern is discussed for neural time series by Ursino et al. (2020), https://doi.org/10.3389/fncom.2020.00045, and applies by analogy to common-mode inflow in filament networks.

### Information-equivalent rate convention

**\(\dot{T}_{\mathrm{fil}}\) is an information-equivalent rate in bits/s, not a raw mass flux.** A raw baryonic mass flux, such as \(\dot{M}_{\mathrm{fil}}\), has units of mass/time and cannot be inserted directly into the TE bound or a dimensionless tightness ratio. If a model uses a relation such as

\[
\dot{T}_{\mathrm{fil}}=\dot{M}_{\mathrm{fil}}\,h(\cdots),
\]

it must define the conversion factor or convention that maps mass flow to information flow and yields units of bits/s. This distinction must remain explicit wherever the filament rate appears in the bound or tightness ratio.

### Cross-scale statistic and power-analysis correction

The proposed statistic is

\[
D_{\mathrm{obs}}=R_{\mathrm{ax}}-R_{\mathrm{fil}},
\]

where the two \(R\) quantities are intended to compare dimensionless tightness ratios, not raw information or mass fluxes. Its interpretation and empirical validity are theoretical.

## 4. Skeptical Perspectives & Alternative Hypotheses
1. **Formal analogy does not imply physical unity.** The shared equations organize a comparison; they do not establish a common mechanism across cortical motor transport and cosmic-web flows.
2. **The TE bound is directional.** Entropy production bounds TE under the stated model conditions; TE does not measure entropy production in reverse.
3. **Markovianity is an assumption to test.** Its suitability for axonal transport and for coarse-grained filament flow is model-dependent.
4. **TE is vulnerable to confounding.** Common input can make predictive dependence appear to be directed coupling. Neural TE concerns are documented by Ursino et al. (2020), https://doi.org/10.3389/fncom.2020.00045.
5. **The scales and observations are not commensurate by default.** There is no unique coarse-graining across about 40 orders of magnitude, no in-vivo FD measurement of axonal transport, and the cosmic-web TE analysis is simulation-only in this framework.
6. **Universality is not assured.** Scale-free network behavior is not ubiquitous (Broido & Clauset, 2019, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08746-5).
7. **Cosmological alternatives remain model-dependent.** CPL parameterization affects the interpretation of dynamical-dark-energy constraints; a parameter fit is not, by itself, evidence that the cross-scale hypothesis is correct.

The cross-scale statistic \(D_{\mathrm{obs}}\), thermodynamic-universality hypothesis \(H_3\), tightness of the entropy-production bound in either system, and gravitational FDT for filaments remain theoretical proposals.
